claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model should be certified for release because current aggregate readiness is above threshold, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the regressed mental-health referral-routing subgroup weakness can be handled through explicit current-release disclosure and monitoring.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if the material segment weakness is explicitly disclosed in current release documentation or covered by an approved mitigation.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may inform context but cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not sufficient if the required current-release disclosure or mitigation predicate is unresolved.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or equivalent release documentation showing the current evaluation results and explicit disclosure of the mental-health referral-routing weakness.
Provide the approval record for any mitigation or risk acceptance covering this subgroup regression in the current release.
Provide the exact launch-readiness threshold reference and the underlying evidence for the stated 2.1 percentage-point aggregate pass.
Provide the launch rehearsal record confirming no severity-one incidents and its scope relative to the affected subgroup behavior.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires that current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and that material segment weaknesses be disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation; the actor summary does not establish that this predicate is actually satisfied.

The mental-health referral-routing slice is described as a material current-release regression below the warning threshold, which makes disclosure or approved mitigation a required support link rather than a caveat.

The actor appropriately treats prior approval and the informal monitoring note as context only, but the packet still appears to rely on a proposed documentation posture without evidence that the documentation or reviewed mitigation exists now.
Public governance guidance can support process expectations, but it does not by itself prove compliance with the internal certification policy for this release.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently supportable on the available record rather than only conditionally supportable if current-release disclosure or approved mitigation is confirmed.
That the subgroup weakness is already explicitly reflected in current release documentation or covered by approved mitigation.
That monitoring at launch is sufficient, absent evidence of reviewed risk acceptance or an approved mitigation tied to the current regression.
